READY/ FIELD NOTES

CHECK THE EVERYDAY DEPENDENCIES.

Practical checks for your home and business. Read the answer, try a free tool, then write down what needs doing.

READY/ Editorial · 2 November 2026 · Independent planning aids

Digital landlines and telecare: ask about the whole connection

A working telephone does not establish that a care alarm will work after a line change or during a power cut. Ask both providers to confirm the arrangement.

READ THE FIELD NOTE →

Food rotation: keep the date wording and the opening instructions

“Expires Friday” loses useful information. Record whether the label says use-by or best before, and read what changes after opening.

READ THE FIELD NOTE →

E-bike charging: plan the place and the time together

The nearest socket is not the whole charging plan. Check the escape route, charger and a routine that keeps charging attended.

READ THE FIELD NOTE →

Flooded road? Plan the delay instead of a depth test

An alternative route, a contact and permission to postpone are more useful than trying to judge whether floodwater is passable.

READ THE FIELD NOTE →

Your backup completed. Can you restore the file you need?

A small restore exercise can reveal whether a business can recover a usable document, who can do it and which parts remain untested.

READ THE FIELD NOTE →

Backup equipment: an open door does not make indoor combustion safe

A camping stove or generator is not automatically a household fallback. Check where it can be used safely before including it in a power-cut plan.

READ THE FIELD NOTE →

Your pet is microchipped. Can the database still reach you?

A chip number identifies a record; it does not track a pet’s location. Check the database and current contact details as their own task.

READ THE FIELD NOTE →

Repeat medicines: plan the supply route before the last dose

For households in England, distinguish routine ordering from urgent supply and keep the relevant pharmacy and NHS routes easy to find.

READ THE FIELD NOTE →

A supplier changes bank details: verify the change outside the message

A familiar invoice or email thread is not enough to establish a payment change. Give a small business a clear verification and approval process.

READ THE FIELD NOTE →

Emergency Alerts are not ordinary texts: check which devices can receive them

Understand the difference between a mobile-network broadcast and a message sent to a phone number, then agree another route for official updates.

READ THE FIELD NOTE →

Boil water, do not drink, do not use: read the instruction before choosing a response

Three water notices require different decisions. Make a short record of the actual instruction, affected uses and next update.

READ THE FIELD NOTE →

A yellow weather warning is a starting point, not your finished decision

Read the place, timing, impacts and likelihood, then record the decision that applies to your own plans.

READ THE FIELD NOTE →

On a Priority Services Register? Confirm the support, contacts and follow-up

Turn “we are registered” into a clear record of which organisations hold your details and what help has actually been discussed.

READ THE FIELD NOTE →

Live in a flat? Get the fire plan for your building, not a generic checklist

Ask for the current building-specific instructions and turn the answer into a clear, accessible household record.

READ THE FIELD NOTE →

Period products belong in the plan: preference, washing and disposal

Make a private, product-specific supply plan that people will actually be comfortable using.

READ THE FIELD NOTE →

Gas heating, electric controls: check what your home actually needs

Map the hidden power dependencies behind heating, internet and everyday routines, then make a practical household fallback plan.

New home? Make a systems map before you need one

A practical walkthrough for locating water controls, household equipment and useful contacts without turning moving day into a technical survey.

Your three-day drinking-water number is only the first decision

Calculate a drinking-water baseline, count what you already have and make a workable storage plan for your own household.

Build a no-cook cupboard from meals you already eat

Turn familiar shelf-stable food into a practical no-cook meal plan, checking portions, opening instructions and leftovers before buying more.

If you cannot get home: agree the household handover in advance

Agree collection responsibilities, contact details and safe alternatives before a delayed journey becomes a household coordination problem.

Card terminal down? Map the decisions before you promise a workaround

A practical downtime exercise for small businesses: identify payment dependencies, ask the provider the right questions and decide who can pause trading.
